(2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same failure mode in src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py: when the SSE reconnection loop in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the pending caller is never notified and hangs forever (previously the code just logged at debug and returned). #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) addressed to the specific request's id and pushing it onto ctx.read_stream_writer, resolving only the affected pending request. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError, which anyio wraps in an ExceptionGroup, requiring a new _unwrap_exception helper to dig the original error back out — a more invasive approach that propagates a fatal error at the task-group/transport level rather than resolving just the one affected request. prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (substring/space-split) to extract auth-param fields, which breaks when a header contains commas inside quoted values or multiple auth schemes/challenges — causing values from one challenge or quoted string to bleed into another field's match. Both PRs fix this by replacing naive parsing with a quote-aware, comma-delimited tokenizer for the header (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012, _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041). (2 PRs)

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same failure mode in src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py: when the SSE reconnection loop in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the pending caller is never notified and hangs forever (previously the code just logged at debug and returned). #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) addressed to the specific request's id and pushing it onto ctx.read_stream_writer, resolving only the affected pending request. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError, which anyio wraps in an ExceptionGroup, requiring a new _unwrap_exception helper to dig the original error back out — a more invasive approach that propagates a fatal error at the task-group/transport level rather than resolving just the one affected request. clusters.pick_reason: Both add nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic to src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py, but #3041 goes a step further with _extract_bearer_auth_params, which restricts extraction to the Bearer scheme's own segment. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only splits everything after the first space into a flat param list, so on a header with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer resource_metadata=y') it would still fail to scope matching to the Bearer challenge specifically — the same substring/cross-challenge bleed the PRs are meant to fix. #3041's scheme-scoped extraction is the more complete fix for the underlying bug.

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After tokens are loaded from persistent storage (e.g. process restart), `token_expiry_time` is never recomputed/restored, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired token as valid, the proactive-refresh path is skipped, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of silently refreshing. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `context.update_token_expiry()` right after loading stored tokens, so `expires_in`/`token_expiry_time` are correct everywhere downstream (including the existing proactive-refresh branch). #2875's own inline comment describes the exact same root cause ('a provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time... proactive-refresh branch above is skipped') but instead patches the symptom by inserting a new reactive 'Step 3.5' refresh-before-reauth branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler. (2 PRs)

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same failure mode in src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py: when the SSE reconnection loop in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the pending caller is never notified and hangs forever (previously the code just logged at debug and returned). #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) addressed to the specific request's id and pushing it onto ctx.read_stream_writer, resolving only the affected pending request. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError, which anyio wraps in an ExceptionGroup, requiring a new _unwrap_exception helper to dig the original error back out — a more invasive approach that propagates a fatal error at the task-group/transport level rather than resolving just the one affected request. members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs edit the exact same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages that governs behavior when an assistant tool_use is not followed by a tool_result — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually-exclusive ways. #2962 gates the whole mismatch-check block on `has_tool_results`, so when a tool_use has no following tool_result at all, no ValueError is raised (treated as valid per spec). #3053 keeps the original gating and instead adds an explicit `raise ValueError("tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks")` in that same case — i.e. it still errors, just with a clearer message. Only one behavior can ship for this code path. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both add nearly identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic to src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py, but #3041 goes a step further with _extract_bearer_auth_params, which restricts extraction to the Bearer scheme's own segment. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only splits everything after the first space into a flat param list, so on a header with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer resource_metadata=y') it would still fail to scope matching to the Bearer challenge specifically — the same substring/cross-challenge bleed the PRs are meant to fix. #3041's scheme-scoped extraction is the more complete fix for the underlying bug.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (substring/space-split) to extract auth-param fields, which breaks when a header contains commas inside quoted values or multiple auth schemes/challenges — causing values from one challenge or quoted string to bleed into another field's match. Both PRs fix this by replacing naive parsing with a quote-aware, comma-delimited tokenizer for the header (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012, _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041).
